citation.title: Diverse Topology Optimization using Modulated Neural Fields
citation.authors: Andreas Radler, Eric Volkmann, Johannes Brandstetter, Arturs Berzins

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: For the MBB beam, generating diverse designs takes TOM 6.1 minutes versus 55.5 minutes for the classical deflated-barrier method.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: [inferred] Table 1 MBB wall times: classical DB 55.5 min divided by TOM 6.1 min = 9.0983606557.
claim.alternatives: Table 1 cantilever: DB 123 min versus TOM 29 min. Bracket: single-solution FeniTop 187 min versus TOM 47 min, but DB was omitted. Introduction qualitatively says TOM is substantially faster than prior methods.

baseline.classical_method: Deflated barrier (DB) for diverse solutions; FeniTop SIMP for a single reference solution (Section 4.2)
baseline.implementation: Public DB implementation with adaptive mesh refinement; FeniTop Python wrapper of FenicsX/DolfinX (Sections 4.2, 4.4)
baseline.solver: FenicsX/DolfinX finite-element solver; linear-system algorithm not stated (Sections 4.2–4.3)
baseline.hardware_classical: Xeon Gold 6150, 36 cores at 2.70 GHz; node has NVIDIA Titan V12 GPU and 384 GB RAM (Appendix A.3)
baseline.hardware_ml: Same experimental node; CPU-parallel FEM and NVIDIA Titan V12 GPU for neural/diversity calculations (Section 3.1, Appendix A.3)
baseline.problem_size: MBB 180 x 60 FEM mesh for TOM; DB 50 x 150 then refined to 27,174 elements; cantilever TOM 150 x 100; bracket TOM 104 x 172 x 60 (Table 2)
baseline.classical_iterations: DB 400 iterations (MBB) and 1,000 (cantilever); FeniTop 400 on each benchmark (Table 2)
baseline.classical_time: DB 55.5 min MBB and 123 min cantilever; FeniTop 2 min MBB, 4 min cantilever, 187 min bracket (Table 1)
baseline.ml_time: TOM optimization 6.1 min MBB, 29 min cantilever, 47 min bracket (Table 1)
baseline.training_time: No offline training; per-problem optimization times are the TOM times in Table 1 (Sections 3.1, 4.4)
baseline.data_generation_cost: No offline dataset for TOM (abstract; Section 3.1)
baseline.quality_metric: Compliance and volume recomputed with common high-resolution FenicsX evaluation mesh; load violation rate and diversity (Section 4.3, Table 1)
baseline.quality_gap: MBB mean compliance 0.75 ± 0.03 for TOM versus 0.67 ± 0.01 for DB; mean volume 55.08 ± 1.04% versus 53.49 ± 0.00% (Table 1)

R1.evidence: Table 1 MBB compares 6.1 versus 55.5 minutes, while TOM has worse mean compliance (0.75 versus 0.67) and a different volume (55.08% versus 53.49%); no time or quality matching is attempted.

R2.evidence: Section 4.4 attributes part of DB's slower runtime to its public implementation's mesh refinement; Table 2 shows DB changes mesh during optimization, but no matched strong-baseline timing is given.

R3.evidence: Abstract and Section 3.1 describe data-free, solver-in-the-loop training separately for each topology problem; its full optimization time is in Table 1.

R4.evidence: Section 4.3 and Table 1 FE-verify returned compliance and report volume and load-violation rates. Section 4.4 notes disconnected floaters in TOM outputs but gives no rate for them.

reporting.n_test_cases: 3 benchmark problems (MBB beam, cantilever, jet-engine bracket; Table 1)

notes: Section 4.2 omits DB and TopoDiff from the 3D bracket comparison. Table 1 filters load-violating designs from quality statistics. Code URL is in the abstract footnote: https://github.com/ml-jku/Topology-Optimization-Modulated-Neural-Fields .
